disclaimer: Curated offline snapshot of public NASA Human Research Program pages. Quotes are verbatim; descriptions are Dr G Zero's paraphrase. Links between Dr G Zero measurements and NASA risks explain why Dr G Zero monitors a measurement. They do not establish that an astronaut is experiencing a risk, they are not diagnoses, and they do not imply NASA endorsement of Dr G Zero.

risks.name: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
risks.formalName: Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload
risks.description: Sleep loss, disrupted circadian rhythms and heavy workload are common in spaceflight. NASA links them to fatigue, errors and reduced performance, and notes that the cabin environment itself (noise, temperature, vibration, light) can make sleep harder.

statements.quote: astronauts commonly experience sleep deprivation
environmental factors (e.g., noise, temperature, vibration, and light) inhibit sleep
16 sunrises and sunsets

indicators.label: Performance decrements and errors (vigilance, reaction time)

signalLinks.rationale: NASA names sleep loss directly; nightly sleep duration is its most direct measure.
Disturbed sleep (time awake in bed) is part of sleep loss; efficiency is Dr G Zero's way of quantifying it.
Self-rated sleep quality is a subjective view of the sleep loss NASA describes.
NASA states that sleep loss and circadian disturbance lead to fatigue.
Composite fatigue estimate derived by Dr G Zero; fatigue itself is named by NASA.
NASA describes performance decrements and errors; reaction time is Dr G Zero's measurable proxy.
Attention lapses are Dr G Zero's proxy for the errors NASA associates with fatigue.
Optional game reaction times may reflect alertness; uncontrolled conditions make this a weak, exploratory proxy.
Dr G Zero hypothesis: lower overnight HRV may accompany poor sleep. Not stated on the NASA pages.

missingMeasurements: Circadian phase markers (e.g. light exposure, sleep timing relative to schedule)
Cabin noise, temperature, vibration and light levels

detectionMethods.description: Compares recent sleep with the astronaut's own days 10–37 baseline.
SCND treats a domain as sustained only when all three detectors agree.
Variability of sleep onset/offset across days. Not implemented; Dr G Zero has no sleep-timing signal.

mitigations.summary: Lighting that simulates Earth's light-dark cycle
mitigations.quote: light-emitting diodes, or LEDs, simulate Earth’s light-dark cycle to help astronauts sleep better

mitigations.summary: Scheduled time for relaxation and self-care
mitigations.quote: designated times for relaxation and self-care

limitations: Dr G Zero's sleep values are simulated wearable/self-report estimates, not polysomnography.
No circadian-phase or workload data, both of which NASA names as contributors.
NASA does not publish thresholds for these consumer-style measures; Dr G Zero compares only with each astronaut's own baseline.

risks.name: Risk of behavioral changes and psychiatric disorders
risks.formalName: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders Leading to In-mission Health and Performance and Long-term Health Effects
risks.description: Isolation and confinement during long missions can lead to changes in cognitive and behavioural functioning. NASA reports that selection, training and ISS countermeasures have mainly been successful, but that countermeasures for exploration-class missions have not yet been validated.

statements.quote: decrements in cognitive and behavioral functioning
have mainly been successful in mitigating this risk
Feasible and acceptable countermeasures for exploration class missions have not yet been developed and validated
Privacy is also a top priority

indicators.label: Sleep (Dr G Zero tracks this under the sleep risk)
Clinical assessment by behavioural health professionals

signalLinks.rationale: NASA names decrements in cognitive functioning; reaction time is one measurable aspect.
Working-memory accuracy is Dr G Zero's operationalisation of cognitive functioning.
Self-rated concentration is a subjective view of cognitive functioning.
Optional games are played for fun under uncontrolled conditions; any link is exploratory.
Optional games are played for fun under uncontrolled conditions; any link is exploratory.
NASA mentions impacts on morale; a mood rating is Dr G Zero's self-report proxy. It is not a depression measure.
Self-rated motivation is Dr G Zero's proxy for the morale NASA mentions.
Dr G Zero hypothesis: perceived stress may accompany behavioural-health strain. Not a NASA-specified indicator on these pages.
NASA names isolation and confinement as the stressor; perceived isolation is Dr G Zero's self-report.
Dr G Zero hypothesis: fatigue co-varies with behavioural strain. NASA links fatigue to the sleep risk.

missingMeasurements: Clinical behavioural-health assessment (only qualified humans can make one)
Validated psychological instruments administered by professionals
Team interaction data (see the teamwork risk)

detectionMethods.description: Deterministic YES / NO / INSUFFICIENT DATA from sustained, multi-detector deviation against the personal baseline.
Descriptive 7-day changes and relationships between signals, with uncertainty.
Interface only; advisory and never able to change a decision. Not implemented in this phase.

mitigations.summary: Selection, training and ISS behavioural health countermeasures
mitigations.quote: the robust set of behavioral health and performance countermeasures on ISS have mainly been successful in mitigating this risk
NASA encourages astronauts to explore self-care options including keeping a regular journal

limitations: Dr G Zero never diagnoses depression or any psychiatric disorder; these signals are self-reports and task scores.
NASA states exploration-class countermeasures are not yet validated; Dr G Zero's suggestions are not validated countermeasures either.
Self-report is affected by willingness to report, mood at the time of rating and survey fatigue.

risks.name: Risk of inadequate teamwork
risks.formalName: Risk of In-Mission Performance and Behavioral Health Decrements Due to Inadequate Cooperation, Coordination, Communication, and Psychosocial Adaptation within a Team
risks.description: Long missions can strain cooperation, coordination and communication within a crew. NASA reports evidence of occasional conflict and notes that team training and performance are not systematically monitored.

statements.quote: evidence of occasional conflict
Team training and performance are not systematically monitored nor evaluated

signalLinks.rationale: Dr G Zero hypothesis: an individual's sense of isolation may relate to team psychosocial adaptation. It is not a team measure.

missingMeasurements: Communication logs (deliberately not collected, for privacy)

detectionMethods.description: Crew Wellbeing shows team-level participation only, never per person and never linked to health.

limitations: Dr G Zero does not measure team functioning. Voluntary shared activities are a social feature, not a team assessment.
Simulated crewmates' responses are synthetic.

risks.name: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
risks.formalName: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations Contributing to Adverse Mission Performance and Health Outcomes
risks.description: Weightlessness causes cardiovascular deconditioning and remodelling. Low blood pressure on standing (orthostatic intolerance) is a primary concern on return to gravity, and stagnant or reversed flow in the internal jugular vein is an emerging finding.

statements.quote: cardiovascular deconditioning, dysfunction, and remodeling
Orthostatic intolerance
Stagnant or reverse flow in the internal jugular vein

signalLinks.rationale: NASA describes countermeasures to prevent low blood pressure; blood pressure is measured directly.
NASA describes countermeasures to prevent low blood pressure; blood pressure is measured directly.
Heart rate is a basic measure of the cardiovascular function NASA describes.
Resting heart rate is Dr G Zero's proxy for cardiovascular deconditioning.
Dr G Zero hypothesis: HRV reflects autonomic regulation. Not stated on the NASA pages.
NASA states regular exercise helps crews maintain cardiovascular fitness; Dr G Zero tracks adherence.

detectionMethods.description: Monitor-tier alert when the 7-day mean is ≥2 SD in the adverse direction, needing ≥10 baseline points. An Dr G Zero screening rule, not a clinical threshold.

mitigations.summary: Regular exercise and a healthy diet
mitigations.quote: Regular exercise and healthy diets help crews maintain cardiovascular fitness

mitigations.summary: Compression garments and fluid loading before landing
mitigations.quote: Lower-body compression garments and drinking lots of fluids prior to landing can help to prevent low blood pressure

limitations: Dr G Zero has no orthostatic test or vascular imaging, which are central to this risk.
Values are synthetic; the 2 SD monitor rule is Dr G Zero's own screening convention, not a NASA threshold.

risks.name: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
risks.formalName: Risk of Reduced Physical Performance Capabilities Due to Reduced Muscle Size, Strength, and Endurance (Muscle Risk)
risks.description: Microgravity reduces muscle size, strength, endurance and aerobic fitness. ISS data show crews who follow the exercise schedule return with minimal average losses, but individual effects vary substantially, and exploration vehicles may have less exercise capability.

statements.quote: if crew adhere to the exercise schedule and have access to adequate exercise countermeasure systems then on average, they return with minimal losses
average losses to strength and aerobic fitness are 10-12% of pre-mission levels
can vary substantially between individual astronauts

indicators.label: Aerobic fitness (resting heart rate as a proxy)

signalLinks.rationale: NASA describes daily resistance training as the countermeasure; Dr G Zero tracks completion against prescription.
NASA describes daily aerobic exercise as the countermeasure; Dr G Zero tracks completion against prescription.
General activity is Dr G Zero's broader proxy for exercise exposure.
NASA mentions periodic fitness self-evaluations; Dr G Zero's weekly fitness test is a simulated equivalent.
Resting heart rate is a rough proxy for the aerobic fitness NASA describes.
NASA names declining muscle size; estimated lean mass is an indirect proxy.
Estimated muscle mass is an indirect proxy for the muscle size NASA describes.
Estimated skeletal muscle mass is an indirect proxy for muscle size.
Segmental estimates are Dr G Zero's illustration of where losses might appear; not a NASA-specified measure.
Segmental estimates are Dr G Zero's illustration of where losses might appear; not a NASA-specified measure.
Segmental estimates are Dr G Zero's illustration of where losses might appear; not a NASA-specified measure.
Segmental estimates are Dr G Zero's illustration of where losses might appear; not a NASA-specified measure.
Segmental estimates are Dr G Zero's illustration of where losses might appear; not a NASA-specified measure.

detectionMethods.description: Gamification rewards completion up to the prescription; nothing is lost for missed days.
7-day mean vs baseline for measured/derived signals (monitor tier).

mitigations.quote: Six to seven days a week, astronauts on the International Space Station perform resistance training and aerobic exercises for 1.5 hours per day

limitations: Body-composition values are simulated estimates, not DXA or imaging.
NASA's 10–12% average loss is a population figure from ISS; it is not used as a per-person threshold.

risks.name: Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
risks.formalName: Risk of Bone Fracture due to Spaceflight-induced Changes to Bone
risks.description: Weight-bearing bones lose density in microgravity, which can raise fracture risk during and after missions. NASA states that exercise, adequate nutrition and medications are needed as countermeasures, and that long-term effects of exploration missions are uncharacterised.

statements.quote: bones lose between 1% and 1.5% of their density each month during four-to-six-month missions
Countermeasures such as exercise, adequate nutrition, and medications are needed

signalLinks.rationale: NASA describes resistive exercise as helping keep bones strong; Dr G Zero tracks adherence.
Dr G Zero hypothesis: muscle loading relates to bone loading. This is NOT a bone measurement.
Dr G Zero hypothesis: muscle loading relates to bone loading. This is NOT a bone measurement.

missingMeasurements: Bone density scans (NASA performs these before and after flight)

detectionMethods.description: Dr G Zero cannot detect bone change; it can only show whether the exercise countermeasure is being completed.

mitigations.quote: Exercise to reduce the deficits in postflight bone density and strengthen muscle force is an essential component of preventing declines in bone tissue
NASA studies have found that medications like bisphosphonate could help mitigate some spaceflight-induced bone loss

limitations: Dr G Zero measures no bone property. Nothing in Dr G Zero can indicate bone loss.
Medication is listed because NASA reports it; Dr G Zero never suggests medication.

risks.name: Risk of Hypoxia
risks.formalName: Risk of Reduced Crew Health and Performance Due to Hypoxia
risks.description: Future exploration vehicles may use reduced-pressure cabin atmospheres to simplify spacewalk preparation, which raises the risk of mild hypoxia. Cabin depressurisation, life-support failure, toxic exposure or illness can also cause hypoxic exposure.

statements.quote: exposure to mild hypobaric hypoxia
of most concern are the potential effects on the increased intracranial pressure, visual impairment, cognitive performance, sensorimotor dysfunction, oxidative damage, and sleep quality

indicators.label: Cabin pressure and oxygen partial pressure

signalLinks.rationale: NASA describes low tissue oxygen; pulse-oximetry saturation is Dr G Zero's proxy.
NASA describes low tissue oxygen; nightly saturation is Dr G Zero's proxy.
Dr G Zero hypothesis: breathing rate may change with low oxygen. Not stated on the NASA pages.

detectionMethods.description: Monitor-tier alert on sustained adverse deviation; not an acute hypoxia alarm.

limitations: Dr G Zero is not an acute hypoxia alarm and must never be used as one; cabin life-support systems fulfil that role.
The pages describe future atmospheres; the simulated ISS-like mission does not model reduced cabin pressure.

risks.name: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
risks.formalName: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition Causing Decrements in In-Mission Health and Performance and Long-term Health (Food and Nutrition Risk)
risks.description: The space food system must be safe, nutritious and acceptable. Adequate nutrition has been demonstrated for 6-month and limited 1-year missions, but sustaining it on long missions with limited resupply is complex, including avoiding menu fatigue.

statements.quote: Adequate nutrition and safe food have been demonstrated for 6-month missions and limited 1-year missions
varied enough to avoid menu fatigue

signalLinks.rationale: Dr G Zero hypothesis: sustained mass change may reflect energy balance. Not stated on these NASA pages.
Dr G Zero hypothesis: fat mass may reflect energy balance.
Dr G Zero hypothesis: body water estimates relate to fluid intake.
Dr G Zero hypothesis: fluid intake is part of nutrition. Not stated on these NASA pages.
Dr G Zero hypothesis: derived hydration estimate.
Dr G Zero hypothesis: glucose is a metabolic marker; not stated on these NASA pages.

detectionMethods.description: 7-day mean vs personal baseline for measured/derived signals.

mitigations.summary: Crew evaluate and choose preferred foods before flight
mitigations.quote: Astronauts work with scientists to evaluate and select their preferred foods before their mission

limitations: Every Dr G Zero link to this risk is an Dr G Zero hypothesis; NASA's pages do not name these measures.
Dr G Zero records no diet, so it cannot assess nutrition.

risks.name: Risk of Altered Immune System Responses
risks.formalName: Risk of In Mission Impacts, Adverse Health Events or Long-Term Health Impacts due to Altered Immune Response (Immune Risk)
risks.description: Spaceflight alters immune function and latent viruses can reactivate, but it is not yet clear whether this increases susceptibility to disease. NASA studies blood, saliva and urine samples, including inflight samples.

statements.quote: it is unclear at present if such alterations lead to increased susceptibility to disease
The reactivation of latent viruses has been documented in crewmembers

indicators.label: Reported symptoms (cold sores, rashes, atypical allergies, infections)

limitations: Dr G Zero measures no immune parameter. Skin temperature is deliberately NOT linked to infection.

risks.name: Risk of Altered Sensorimotor and Vestibular Function
risks.formalName: Risk of Altered Sensorimotor/Vestibular Function Impacting Critical Mission Tasks, Human Health, and Long-Term Health (Sensorimotor Risk)
risks.description: Altered gravity causes motion sickness, spatial disorientation and reduced postural control, locomotion and fine motor control. Readaptation takes hours to days, and impairment is greatest around gravity transitions.

statements.quote: motion sickness, spatial disorientation, decrements in postural control and locomotion, and manual and fine motor control deficits
It takes hours to days for the body to readapt to gravity upon landing

limitations: Dr G Zero does not measure sensorimotor function. Reaction-time tests are not validated sensorimotor measures and are not linked here.

risks.name: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
risks.formalName: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS Risk)
risks.description: Headward fluid shifts in weightlessness can cause optic-nerve swelling, retinal folds, flattening of the back of the eye and brain changes. SANS has no terrestrial equivalent and is a top research priority for long missions.

statements.quote: there is no terrestrial disease equivalent
Approximately 70 percent of astronauts aboard the International Space Station experience some swelling in the back of their eyes

limitations: Dr G Zero measures no ocular or neurological parameter. NASA's investigated countermeasures (supplements, mechanical fluid-shift interventions) are research, not recommendations.

risks.name: Risk of Decompression Sickness
risks.formalName: Risk of Mission Impacts and Long-Term Health Issues due to Decompression Sickness
risks.description: Moving too quickly from higher to lower pressure without enough denitrogenation (for example before a spacewalk) can cause nitrogen bubbles that damage tissues. NASA uses prebreathe protocols and has standards for prevention and treatment.

statements.quote: NASA standards exist for DCS prevention and treatment
The effects of fractional gravity and exploration atmospheres on DCS risk are currently unknown

mitigations.quote: Denitrogenation protocols (removing nitrogen from the body) are employed to minimize the formulation of gas emboli (bubbles) forming during an EVA

limitations: Out of Dr G Zero's scope. Note: the 'HSRB resources' link on NASA's public DCS page pointed to the behavioural-health HSRB page when retrieved; Dr G Zero cites the DCS HSRB page directly.

risks.name: Risk of Host-Microorganism Interactions
risks.formalName: Risk of Adverse Health Effects Due to Host-Microorganism Interactions
risks.description: Astronauts' skin and gut microbial communities change in space and some microbes appear more virulent, but how this affects disease risk is unknown. Preventive measures limit, but cannot fully prevent, infection.

statements.quote: microbial infection of astronauts cannot be completely prevented and does occur

mitigations.summary: Limiting crew exposure to large groups before launch
mitigations.quote: limiting flight crew exposure to large groups in the two weeks prior to launch

limitations: Out of Dr G Zero's scope.

risks.name: Risk of Injury and Compromised Performance from Spacewalks
risks.formalName: Risk of Mission Impacting Injury and Compromised Performance and Long-Term Health Effects due to EVA Operations (EVA Risk)
risks.description: Spacewalks carry significant physical and mental demands and injury risk, which will increase as exploration spacewalks become more frequent and longer.

statements.quote: spacewalks will occur more frequently and last longer, creating new physical and mental demands

indicators.label: Suit injuries, EVA workload and duration

mitigations.quote: Researchers have created “prebreathe protocols” to ensure crew members are exposed to high levels of oxygen before spacewalks

limitations: The simulated mission contains no spacewalks.

risks.name: Risk of injury from dynamic loads
risks.formalName: Risk of In-Mission Injury and Performance Decrements and Long-term Health Effects due to Dynamic Loads (Dynamic Loads Risk)
risks.description: Landing and other dynamic phases of flight can injure crew, especially after bone and muscle weakening. NASA notes current standards and tools do not adequately capture the spaceflight environment.

statements.quote: these do not adequately mitigate the risk of injury due to the unique spaceflight environment

indicators.label: Vehicle loads, seating and restraint configuration

limitations: Out of Dr G Zero's scope.

risks.name: Risk of radiation-induced cancers
risks.description: Space radiation increases lifetime cancer risk and may affect other tissues and the central nervous system. Shielding helps against solar particle events but does not mitigate galactic cosmic radiation.

statements.quote: Shielding is effective against some radiation exposure, such as solar particle events (SPE) but does not mitigate Galactic Cosmic Radiation (GCR) exposure

limitations: Dr G Zero has no dosimetry. Cognitive measures are deliberately NOT linked to radiation.

risks.name: Risk of inadequate systems operations support
risks.formalName: Risk of Adverse Mission Outcomes Due to Earth Independent Human-Systems Operations (EIHSO Risk)
risks.description: As missions travel farther from Earth, crews will need to operate and repair systems more independently, without real-time ground support.

statements.quote: as the distance from Earth increases, crew will need to be more independent and be able to handle greater operational complexity

mitigations.quote: Crew members also receive training before a mission to familiarize themselves with various systems and respond to emergencies themselves

limitations: Out of Dr G Zero's scope. Dr G Zero itself aims for an Earth-independent, offline design.
